questions.q: Per this lesson, is an event-driven design automatically the 'more advanced' or 'more correct' choice compared to a synchronous API?
options: Yes, events are always architecturally superior
Yes, but only for high-volume platform events
No, batch processing should always be preferred over both
No — synchronous APIs, events, and batch processing are three different tools suited to different situations, not tiers of sophistication
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns against treating events as inherently more advanced — a real architecture review expects a justified choice based on the requirement, not a default preference for events.

questions.q: A checkout page needs to confirm a shipping address is valid before letting the customer submit an order. Which approach fits best, and why?
options: A platform event, because fan-out is always preferable
A synchronous API callout, because the user is waiting and needs exactly one direct answer right now
Scheduled batch processing, run nightly
Change Data Capture, since the address is a field on a record
questions.explain: When a caller needs an immediate answer to continue, a synchronous API fits — an event-driven design would force an artificial polling or callback mechanism to recreate what a direct call already provides.

questions.q: Recalculating every account's loyalty tier once a night, regardless of what did or didn't happen that day, is an example of which approach?
options: A custom platform event triggered by a Flow
Change Data Capture on the Account object
Scheduled batch processing (Batch Apex / Scheduled Apex), since there's no single triggering fact to publish an event about
A synchronous REST API call from an external system
questions.explain: Work that must happen on a schedule independent of any specific triggering fact is scheduled batch processing, not an event — there's no discrete 'thing that happened' for an event to announce.

questions.q: Why is publishing ten thousand individual events for one nightly bulk data load usually a design smell?
options: Because platform events cannot be published in bulk at all
Because CDC cannot be enabled on objects touched by a data load
Because ten thousand events always exceeds the org's daily allocation
Because events are meant to model discrete, individually-meaningful facts, not bulk data movement — the real requirement is likely a batch job
questions.explain: Events model individually meaningful facts. A bulk, periodic operation disguised as thousands of events is usually a sign the real requirement is scheduled batch processing instead.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should a strong justification for an integration-style choice include in an architecture review?
options: Which specific decision-framework question drove the choice, and an acknowledgment of what the chosen approach gives up
A claim that the chosen approach is the newest technology available
Only the name of the Salesforce feature used, with no further explanation
A guarantee that the design requires no monitoring
questions.explain: The lesson calls for naming the deciding question and acknowledging the trade-off given up (decoupling, immediate confirmation, or real-time responsiveness) — a design that can't articulate the cost usually hasn't fully reasoned through it.
